name: ContentReferenceProfile
title: ContentReference Profile
description: A profile on the element identified by the contentReference that also applies to this element.

element.short: Profile (element) that also applies to this element
element.definition: A profile on the element identified by the contentReference that also applies to this element.
element.comment: This extension is used to reuse existing constraints. The most common reason is to apply a profile recursively - e.g. so that the constraints a profile makes on Questionnaire.item also apply to Questionnaire.item.item. This is similar to ElementDefinition.type.profile, but it applies to the contentReference: the profile is applied on the target of the contentReference, not on the source of the reference (this is due to the way contentReference works). The value refers to an element definition in a profile, not to the profile itself, using the same format as the contentReference (a canonical URL for the profile, followed by '#' and the element id). The reference would usually be to the element's parent, so that the constraints are applied recursively, but other patterns are possible.

element.short: identifies the meaning of the extension
element.definition: Source of the definition for the extension code - a logical name or a URL.
element.comment: The definition may point directly to a computable or human-readable definition of the extensibility codes, or it may be a logical URI as declared in some other specification. The definition SHALL be a URI for the Structure Definition defining the extension.

element.definition: Value of extension - must be one of a constrained set of the data types (see [Extensibility](http://hl7.org/fhir/R5/extensibility.html) for a list).
